text:
leah_morris: starting thread for MeridianSystems POC commit. Sales wants a compact, conservative capacity recommendation and a pasteable autoscale snippet for the SOW. traffic profile below.

dan_zhao: profile: steady 28 rps, bursts to 320 rps for ~90s twice/day. avg 360 tokens, heavy tails to 1100. model planned: M-Large quantized.

oliver_kwon: perf estimate: use 9k tokens/s per A100-equivalent for planning. steady tokens/s = 28*360 = 10_080 -> ~1.12 -> baseline 2 GPUs. bursts peak ~352k t/s -> ~39 GPUs peak (need autoscale).

leah_morris: sales asks conservative commit number for billing + AZ tolerance. ops rec?

oliver_kwon: recommend reserved=5 (about 4-5x steady) pinned across 2 AZs, min_gpus=1 to keep warm, burst_credit_pool for short spikes, and preheat KV seed of top-20% prefixes. gives good p95 SLA without overcommitting.

dan_zhao: pasteable autoscale snippet for SOW: ```autoscale_policy:
reserved_gpus: 5
min_gpus: 1
burst_credit_tokens: 1600
scale_up_condition: p95_latency_ms > 350 OR queue_depth > 50
scale_down_condition: p95_latency_ms < 220 for 6m
preheat_strategy: kv_seed_top20% (synthetic, no PII)
az_affinity: spread_across=2
```

leah_morris: security question: one-liner confirming preheat doesn't use customer data?

security-bot: one-liner: "KV preheat jobs use anonymized synthetic prefixes and, for Dedicated/Private deployments, run inside the customer's network boundary; no customer PII is uploaded to Redwood-managed preheat jobs."

oliver_kwon: cost tradeoff quick lines for deck: reserve2=lower commit but higher variable spend and less predictable p95; reserve5=higher commit, stable p95, AZ tolerance; reserve1+burst=lowest commit, highest variable spend and latency variability.

leah_morris: action items: (1) oliver run short sim for reserve2 vs reserve5 numbers and post (2) dan add snippet & security one-liner to SOW draft. will update sales in 12h. :thumbsup:
